question: The Vardhan dynasty, was also known by which of the following names? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Gupta dynasty
Pushyabhuti dynasty
Nanda dynasty
Maurya dynasty
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pushyabhuti dynasty

Explanation:
The Vardhan dynasty was also known as the Pushyabhuti dynasty. It was established in the late 6th century in northern India with its capital at Thanesar (present-day Haryana). The founder of this dynasty was Pushyabhuti, while the most famous ruler was Harshavardhana (Harsha), who ruled from 606 to 647 CE. Under Harsha's reign, the dynasty reached its zenith and he also made Kannauj his capital. The dynasty is mentioned in Harshacharita, written by Banabhatta. After Harsha's death, the dynasty declined.

☛ Alternative name of Vardhan dynasty → Pushyabhuti dynasty
☛ Capital of Vardhan dynasty → Thanesar (early)
☛ Most famous ruler of Vardhan dynasty → Harshavardhana
☛ Court poet of Harshavardhana → Banabhatta
☛ Chinese traveler during Harsha's period → Hiuen Tsang
question_hi: वर्धन वंश को निम्नलिखित में से किस नाम से भी जाना जाता था? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: गुप्त वंश
पुष्यभूति वंश
नंद वंश
मौर्य वंश
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है पुष्यभूति वंश

Explanation:
वर्धन वंश को पुष्यभूति वंश के नाम से भी जाना जाता था। यह वंश छठी शताब्दी के उत्तरार्ध में उत्तर भारत में स्थापित हुआ था, जिसकी राजधानी थानेसर (वर्तमान हरियाणा) थी। इस वंश के संस्थापक पुष्यभूति थे, जबकि सबसे प्रसिद्ध शासक हर्षवर्धन (हर्ष) थे, जिन्होंने 606 से 647 ई. तक शासन किया। हर्षवर्धन के शासनकाल में यह वंश अपने चरम पर था और उसने कन्नौज को भी अपनी राजधानी बनाया। इस वंश का उल्लेख बाणभट्ट द्वारा रचित हर्षचरित में मिलता है। हर्षवर्धन के बाद इस वंश का पतन हुआ।

question: The term gomat in the Rigveda refers to which of the following?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (14/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: A warrior
A priest
A wealthy person
A milkmaid
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A wealthy person

Explanation:
The term 'gomat' in the Rigveda refers to a person who owns cows. In ancient Indian society, cows were considered a symbol of wealth. The more cows a person had, the wealthier they were considered. Therefore, 'gomat' means a wealthy person. The word is derived from 'go' (cow) and 'mat' (wealthy/owner). It is used multiple times in the Rigveda to denote economic status. It does not refer to a warrior, priest, or milkmaid.

☛ Meaning of gomat → Wealthy person or cow owner
☛ Which Veda contains the term gomat → Rigveda
☛ Main measure of wealth in ancient India → Number of cows
☛ Meaning of 'go' → Cow or Earth
☛ Other 'go' related terms in Rigveda → Gavishthi (battle), Gopati (protector)
question_hi: ऋग्वेद में 'गोमत' शब्द निम्नलिखित में से किसे संदर्भित करता है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (14/08/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: एक योद्धा
एक पुजारी
एक धनी व्यक्ति
एक दूधवाली
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है एक धनी व्यक्ति

Explanation:
ऋग्वेद में 'गोमत' शब्द का प्रयोग उस व्यक्ति के लिए किया गया है जो गायों का मालिक होता है। प्राचीन भारतीय समाज में गायों को धन का प्रतीक माना जाता था। गायों की संख्या जितनी अधिक होती थी, व्यक्ति उतना ही धनी माना जाता था। इसलिए 'गोमत' शब्द का तात्पर्य एक धनी व्यक्ति से है। यह शब्द 'गो' (गाय) और 'मत' (धनी/मालिक) से मिलकर बना है। ऋग्वेद में कई स्थानों पर इस शब्द का उल्लेख हुआ है, जो समाज में आर्थिक स्थिति को दर्शाता है। यह किसी योद्धा, पुजारी या दूधवाली के लिए प्रयुक्त नहीं होता था।

question: Which of the following officials toured Mauryan provinces every five years to inspect administration and submit reports on provincial governance? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (14/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Rajuka
Pradeshika
Nagarika
Amatya
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pradeshika

Explanation:
In the Mauryan administration, there were three categories of officials: Pradeshika, Rajuka, and Nagarika. The Pradeshika was a high-ranking officer who toured the provinces every five years to inspect the administration and submit reports on provincial governance. This tour was primarily meant for review and reporting. The Rajuka was responsible for judicial matters and land measurement. The Nagarika was in charge of city administration. Amatya were ministers or high-ranking officials. Thus, the task of provincial inspection was assigned to the Pradeshika.

☛ Mauryan official for provincial inspection → Pradeshika
☛ Interval of Pradeshika's tour → Five years
☛ Main duty of Rajuka → Justice and land measurement
☛ Nagarika's jurisdiction → City administration

Explanation:

question: What is the main content of the four Vedas composed during the Early Vedic period? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: War strategies
Agricultural manuals
Laws and rituals
Prayers and hymns
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Prayers and hymns

Explanation:
The four Vedas – Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda – composed during the Early Vedic period primarily contain prayers and hymns. The Rigveda consists of hymns praising deities, the Yajurveda includes sacrificial formulas and rituals, the Samaveda is a collection of melodies for chanting, and the Atharvaveda contains spells and charms for daily life. These texts are centered on religious worship and rituals, not on war strategies, agricultural manuals, or legal codes. Thus, the correct answer is ‘Prayers and hymns’.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Oldest Veda → Rigveda
☛ Number of Vedas → Four
☛ Main subject of Samaveda → Music and chanting
☛ Yajurveda is related to → Sacrificial rituals
☛ Atharvaveda primarily contains → Domestic and medicinal spells

question: Which of the following texts is considered the earliest Tamil grammar work? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Tolkappiyam
Silappadikaram
Manimekalai
Kural
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tolkappiyam

Explanation:
Tolkappiyam is considered the earliest Tamil grammar work. It was composed during the Sangam period (approximately 500 BCE to 300 CE). Its author is Tolkappiyar. This text provides a detailed description of Tamil phonology, word formation, sentence structure, and semantics. Tolkappiyam is divided into three books: Eluttadikaram (sounds), Soladikaram (words), and Poruladikaram (meaning/subject matter). It is the foundation of Tamil literature and served as a basis for all later Tamil grammar works. The text is highly revered in Tamil culture and is one of the oldest extant Indian linguistic works.

☛ To which period does Tolkappiyam belong? → Sangam period
☛ How many books are in Tolkappiyam? → Three (Eluttadikaram, Soladikaram, Poruladikaram)
☛ What is the oldest extant Tamil grammar work? → Tolkappiyam
☛ What is the subject of Tolkappiyam? → Tamil grammar and poetics

question: In Jain religion, the Svetarnbara canon consists of how many of Agamas? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: 6
12
35
45
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 45

Explanation:
In the Svetambara tradition of Jainism, the canonical literature consists of 45 Agamas. These Agamas are the scriptures containing the teachings of Mahavira and were compiled by the Ganadharas. The Svetambara canon includes 12 Angas, 12 Upangas, 10 Prakirnakas, 6 Chedasutras, 4 Mulasutras, and 1 Chulika. In contrast, the Digambara sect accepts only the 12 Angas as authoritative. The Svetambara Agamas cover ethics, philosophy, conduct, and karma theory, and are considered the most authentic source of Jain doctrine in the Svetambara tradition.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Total number in the Svetambara canon → 45
☛ Number of Agamas accepted by Digambaras → 12 (Angas)
☛ Main divisions of Svetambara Agamas → 12 Angas, 12 Upangas, 10 Prakirnakas, 6 Chedasutras, 4 Mulasutras, 1 Chulika
☛ Source of Jain Agamas → Teachings of Mahavira
☛ First Agama in Svetambara tradition → Acharanga Sutra

question: Which of the following Jain councils was held at Vallabhi (Gujarat) in 512 CE under the chairmanship of Devardhi Kshamasramana? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Third
Second
Fourth
First
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Second

Explanation:
The Second Jain Council was held in 512 CE at Vallabhi (Gujarat) under the chairmanship of Devardhi Kshamasramana. Its primary purpose was to compile and preserve the Jain scriptures, particularly the Agamas, in written form. The First Jain Council had been held earlier at Pataliputra around 300 BCE. After the Second Council, the Third Jain Council was also held at Vallabhi in the 5th century. The Second Council is crucial for the Shwetambara sect, as it systematically organized the 12 Angas and Upangas. Devardhi Kshamasramana was a prominent Acharya who contributed significantly to the preservation of Jain literature.

☛ Third Jain Council → Vallabhi, 5th century
☛ Jain Agama texts → 12 Angas, 12 Upangas, 10 Prakirnakas, etc.
☛ Devardhi Kshamasramana → Shwetambara Acharya, compiler of Agamas

question: Which site provides archaeological evidence of the earliest known urban civilisation in the Indian subcontinent with planned city structures?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 1)

question: After the fall of the Mauryan Empire, which dynasty was founded by Pushyamitra Shunga, the general who killed the last Mauryan ruler? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Kanva Dynasty
Satavahana Dynasty
Shunga Dynasty
Gupta Dynasty
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Shunga Dynasty

Explanation:
After the fall of the Mauryan Empire, the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha was killed by his general Pushyamitra Shunga in 185 BCE. Pushyamitra Shunga established the Shunga Dynasty, which lasted from 185 BCE to 73 BCE. The capital of this dynasty was Pataliputra. Pushyamitra Shunga performed the Ashwamedha Yajna and patronized Brahminical religion. During the Shunga period, art and culture flourished, exemplified by the stupas of Bharhut and Sanchi. The last ruler of this dynasty was Devabhuti, who was killed by his minister Vasudeva Kanva, leading to the establishment of the Kanva Dynasty.

question: During the period of medieval Indian literature, which language began to decline as the dominant medium for Buddhist literary expression and scholarship?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 1)

Sanskrit
Apabhramsha
Prakrit
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pali

Explanation:
During the medieval period of Indian literature, Pali began to decline as the dominant medium for Buddhist literary expression and scholarship. question: Which of the following dynasties initiated the practice of land grants to Brahmanas? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 2)

question: Which of the following is cited as evidence for a highly centralised administration in the Indus-Sarasvati civilisation? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Elaborate royal tombs
Absence of seals and standard script
Standardised weights and measures
Monumental palaces and temples
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Standardised weights and measures

Explanation:
The presence of standardised weights and measures in the Indus-Sarasvati civilisation is cited as evidence of a highly centralised administration. These weights and measures were uniform across the entire civilisation area, indicating a centrally controlled system of trade and exchange. The weights were typically made of hard stones like chert or agate, and followed a ratio of 16 (e.g., 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 160, 200, 320, 640, 1600, 3200, 6400, 16000). For measurement, scales made of clay or shell were used. Such standardisation would not have been possible without a strong central government. In contrast, no elaborate royal tombs or monumental palaces have been found, and seals and script did exist.

question: Which of the following is/are an ancient set of inscriptions, promoting moral values and governance principles and is considered one of the earliest written records in Indian history? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 2)

Vedas
Edicts of Ashoka
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Edicts of Ashoka

Explanation:
The Edicts of Ashoka are among the earliest written records in Indian history. They were commissioned by Emperor Ashoka (268–232 BCE), a ruler of the Mauryan dynasty. These inscriptions primarily promote moral values, the principles of Dhamma (righteousness), and governance ideals. They emphasize non-violence, truth, compassion, and social welfare. Found across India and beyond (e.g., Afghanistan), they are written in ancient scripts like Brahmi and Kharosthi. These edicts are crucial sources for understanding ancient Indian history, culture, and the spread of Buddhism. They reflect Ashoka's transformation from a conqueror to a benevolent ruler after the Kalinga war.

question: Which military division had become rare in warfare during the Gupta period despite being part of the army in texts?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 3)

question: The Visuddhimagga, a key Buddhist text, was written by which of the following scholars? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Nagarjuna
Aryadeva
Buddhaghosa
Vasubandhu
solution:

Explanation:
The Visuddhimagga, meaning 'Path of Purification', is a key text in Theravada Buddhism. It was composed by the scholar Buddhaghosa in the 5th century CE. The text systematically summarizes the teachings of the Buddha and provides a detailed commentary on the Abhidhamma. Buddhaghosa is regarded as the greatest commentator of the Theravada tradition, and he also wrote commentaries on the Tripitaka. question: During the Indus Valley Civilisation, the presence of jewellery made from precious metals and semi-precious stones in small-town settings supports the argument that ____. (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:

The discovery of such luxury items in smaller settlements suggests that even non-urban areas had a stratified social structure.

question: Which of the following groups of people is said to have migrated into the late Indus Valley era India from Central Asia? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Dravidas
Mesopotamians
Aryans
Shakas
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Aryans

Explanation:
The Aryans are believed to have migrated from Central Asia into India during the late Indus Valley era, around 1500 BCE. They were pastoral nomads from the steppes of Central Asia who entered the Indian subcontinent through the northwestern passes, settling in the Sapta Sindhu region (land of seven rivers). Their language, Sanskrit, became the foundation of many Indian languages. The arrival of the Aryans led to the development of the Vedic civilization, which laid the basis for the caste system and the Vedic religion. Their sacred texts, the four Vedas (Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda), are considered the cornerstone of Indian culture. In contrast, Dravidians were indigenous to India, Mesopotamians were from the Middle East, and Shakas migrated later from Central Asia.

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है आर्य

Explanation:
आर्यों का मध्य एशिया से भारत आगमन सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता के उत्तरार्ध में हुआ माना जाता है। यह प्रवास लगभग 1500 ईसा पूर्व हुआ, जिसके बाद वैदिक सभ्यता का विकास हुआ। आर्य मूलतः मध्य एशिया के स्टेपी क्षेत्रों के घुमंतू जनजाति थे, जो उत्तर-पश्चिम भारत के दर्रों से होते हुए सप्त सिंधु क्षेत्र में बसे। उनकी भाषा संस्कृत थी, जो भारतीय आर्य भाषाओं की जननी मानी जाती है। आर्यों के आगमन ने भारतीय समाज में वर्ण व्यवस्था और वैदिक धर्म की नींव रखी। उनके ग्रंथ ऋग्वेद, सामवेद, यजुर्वेद और अथर्ववेद भारतीय संस्कृति के आधार माने जाते हैं। द्रविड़ भारत के मूल निवासी थे, मेसोपोटामियाई मध्य पूर्व और शक मध्य एशिया से थे लेकिन बाद में आए।
